We need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups. IR spectrum shows peaks; carbonyl stretch typically around 1700 cm-1 (1650-1750). The given peaks: 1606, 1587, plus many high frequencies (3357 O-H, etc). No peak near 1700. So likely zero carbonyl groups. Could also be conjugated carbonyl lower ~1680, but not present. So answer 0.

Check other data? Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons ~190-210 ppm. But IR suggests none. Use carbon NMR maybe to confirm but not needed. To be safe, maybe check carbon NMR quickly.
